clue.text: Got key cut

parts.note: F is a musical key
etched means cut into a surface, as an engraver does

explanation.surface: Someone reports having had a new key cut at the locksmith's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key cut' reads as one errand, but it splits: the key of F, then ETCHED for 'cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gone and brought something back is to have got it; both are past tenses of retrieving.

clue.text: Coaster taking iron to Italian city

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Lucca is a walled city in Tuscany

explanation.surface: A cargo ship carries iron to a port in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' is a vessel sailing along a coast, not a drinks mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean sailing boat that plies along the coast, a coasting vessel.

clue.text: A wine grower, like St Paul

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine
a grower produces, and so is a maker

explanation.surface: A vineyard owner is compared with the apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: Acts 18 says Paul worked as a maker of tents. Tent is a red wine, so a producer of it is a 'wine grower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Paul supported himself by sewing shelters of cloth or hide, according to Acts.

clue.text: A flighty one, the maiden who married Soames

explanation.surface: A capricious young woman is said to have wed a man called Soames.
explanation.walkthrough: In Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, Soames Forsyte marries Irene, whose maiden name this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird is a flier, and Irene Forsyte's maiden surname in Galsworthy's novels is the same word.

clue.text: The record belonging to us has a note of the conversation

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
ours means belonging to us
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Our record contains a musical note from a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken exchange or discussion between people is talk.

clue.text: Rose and disconnected speaker

explanation.surface: A flower is paired with someone whose talk wanders.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose of a sprawling kind bears this name, and someone who talks disjointedly at length is one too.

clue.text: Concentrate on cutting the hedge

indicators.note: cutting means the hedge loses its first letter

parts.note: privet is a common hedging shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to focus on trimming the hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix the attention or gaze firmly on something, as in being riveted, is to concentrate.

clue.text: Area of hidden danger filmed in Eastern riots

indicators.note: riots suggests disorder, so the letters run wild into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dangerous zone is caught on camera during unrest in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground sown with buried explosives; figuratively any situation full of unseen hazards.

clue.text: A vassal, for example, had to bed down outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for bedding down goes round the next piece

parts.note: to lie is to bed down

explanation.surface: A feudal tenant was made to sleep out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal usage the word could mean a man owing allegiance, as well as the lord owed it.

clue.text: Vitamin C container available in Shropshire out of hours

indicators.note: available suggests something on hand in a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out of means the letters for hours are taken from the county

parts.note: hrs is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: A vitamin supplement can be bought in an English county after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: SHROPSHIRE (an English county) loses H, R, S for 'out of hours', leaving SOPHIRE, rearranged by 'available'.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fruit of the wild rose is rich in ascorbic acid and once made into syrup for it.

clue.text: Solitary individual holding the two sides apart

indicators.note: the two sides are held apart, with something placed between them

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two sides
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A peacemaker stands between two quarrelling factions, keeping them apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' places ONE between L and R, keeping the sides apart; 'holding' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps to themselves and shuns company is a solitary person.

clue.text: A number of letters addressed to main parts of the world

indicators.note: addressed in the sense of spoken, so the letters are heard rather than read

parts.note: seven Cs, a number of copies of the letter C

explanation.surface: A pile of post has been sent to destinations across the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'main' is the sea, an old poetic sense. Seven copies of the letter C, said out loud, give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional phrase for all the world's oceans; 'the main' is a poetic word for the open sea.

clue.text: Striking debut

explanation.surface: Two words a critic might use of an impressive first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who walk out on strike are doing this, and a debutante's formal introduction to society was called this.

clue.text: Saucy novel

explanation.surface: Two words describing a racy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky or impudent behaviour is called this, and something new and original is too.

clue.text: Not straight like the botanic gardens

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
Kew Gardens in west London are the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: The winding paths of a famous garden are being described as crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crooked, set at an angle, is off the true line.

clue.text: Way to tend free-range domestic fowl

indicators.note: free-range suggests roaming loose, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to look after hens allowed to roam outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An American breed of chicken kept by poultry farmers.

clue.text: It illustrates the ups and downs of a country

definitions.text: It illustrates the ups and downs of a country

parts.words: It illustrates the ups and downs of a country
parts.note: reads like a nation's history of fortunes, but means a chart showing hills and valleys in raised form

explanation.surface: Something charts a nation's changing fortunes over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart modelled in raised form shows terrain heights, the literal highs and lows of the land.

clue.text: In bed with a virus, he throws things down anywhere

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
a bug is an infection, a virus

explanation.surface: A sick person in bed tosses things on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drops rubbish in public places carelessly.

clue.text: Joggers in verse, perhaps

parts.note: not runners in a poem but memory joggers, often in rhyme like 'Thirty days hath September'

explanation.surface: Runners described in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory aids, often rhymes, that jog recall of facts.

clue.text: Fine girl destined, they say, for heaven

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
Irma is a girl's name

indicators.note: they say signals that the next word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meant means destined, as in 'meant to be'

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman is said to be bound for paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The vault of the sky, poetically the heavens above.

clue.text: Soft soap for use in face-cloth?

explanation.surface: A gentle soap to use on a washcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattering talk is called this in British slang, and a small square of towelling for washing has the same name.

clue.text: A delusion in the unconscious

parts.note: a false picture that the mind produces while one is asleep

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist describes a false belief buried in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Images and stories experienced during sleep are illusory, produced without conscious control.

clue.text: Runners without money have to cope with the daily grind

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the runners go round the money

parts.note: milers are runners in mile races
L is the abbreviation for pound, money

explanation.surface: Athletes with no cash must face the drudgery of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The definition is cryptic: those who grind corn daily.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work a corn mill literally grind every day, so the definition is a punning description.

clue.text: Refrain from prima donna holding nothing back

indicators.note: holding means the reversed singer contains the next piece
back means the word for the singer is read in reverse

parts.note: a diva is a prima donna, a leading female opera singer
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to stay away from a temperamental soprano who never holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIVA into AVID, and 'holding' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or keep clear of something is to refrain from it.

clue.text: The colon, say, in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark appears in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is a body part, and a newspaper is a mouthpiece of a party or group.

clue.text: Smoother material for bullet-proof vest?

parts.note: an abrasive for polishing, whimsically pictured as metal knitting yarn for armour

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what fabric would make a protective vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of fine metal fibres used to polish and smooth surfaces; the name jokingly suggests a metal knitting yarn.

clue.text: Sea-dogs smelling, perhaps

explanation.surface: Old sailors are noticed for their odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced sailors are old tars, and smelling preparations of ammonium carbonate revive the faint.

clue.text: Mark new sheets and pillowcases

parts.note: a line is a mark drawn on a surface

explanation.surface: Someone labels fresh bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding collectively, traditionally woven from flax.

clue.text: Dark clobber required for this place of entertainment

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
to club someone is to clobber them

explanation.surface: Black clothing is the dress code for a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' looks like the British slang for clothes, but it is the verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue open late for drinking, music and dancing.

clue.text: To have a row in a casino is easy

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Picking a fight at the gaming tables is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with 'cow', is a loud din or racket.

clue.text: Square drill for the cavalry?

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant drills horsemen on the parade square.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille, a dance for four couples in a square, bears this name; so do cavalry soldiers armed with spears.

clue.text: Book I is in production

explanation.surface: A first volume is being prepared for print.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Bible bears this name, and the word also means origin or creation.
